thread:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a short decision on queue governance for the continuous-batching scheduler. Main questions: who owns per-tenant headroom, how do we surface admission vs eviction to the control plane, and what's the interop contract when a request moves between lanes?
aj: +1 to landing something small. can we pick a default that is safe and iterate?
cheng: I sketched three modes in the doc: `per-tenant-microlane`, `global-coalesce-with-credits`, and `hybrid-escrow`. each has tradeoffs for tail latency and fairness.
sam: TL;DR of tradeoffs?
cheng: per-tenant micro lanes = best isolation, worse GPU packing. global coalesce = best throughput, harder to bound long-tail. hybrid = token escrow + soft-fences, middle ground.
maria: We also need an interoperable API for admission/eviction signals so Dedicated/Dedicated-shared clusters can implement different policies without forking runtime. proposal: a small signal set: `reserve(headroom)`, `release(headroom)`, `evict(reason)`, `preemptable=true|false`.
alex: That sounds reasonable. one practical concern: how expensive is `reserve()` to call for each request? we can't add a round-trip to control plane per token.
cheng: reserve is intended as a cheap local op, backed by periodic sync to control plane. think local escrow ledger + heartbeat. only large deltas push to control plane.
maria: ok. then we need the ledger semantics spelled out. my suggestion: escrow decreases on enqueue, increases on completion, and we expose metrics for enforced vs suggested reservations.
aj: about cross-lane moves: if runtime moves a request from coalesce-lane -> isolation-lane, who pays the headroom difference? my vote: runtime pays transient delta and emits an allocation event so billing/telemetry can reconcile.
sam: runtime-paying transient delta seems simplest, but we should add a guard: if delta exceeds X% of tenant's quota, reject the move and log an incident.
cheng: agreed. also we should add a lightweight wire format for the events, e.g. JSON blob:```
{
  "event":"allocation_change",
  "tenant_id":"t-123",
  "prev_lane":"coalesce",
  "new_lane":"isolated",
  "delta_headroom":256
}
```
alex: looks fine. does this tie into Optimize (recommendations)? we could let Optimize suggest `X%` thresholds per tenant.
maria: yes, tie-in encouraged. final open item: default eviction policy. my draft: `evict(oldest_soft, then_largest)` — i.e., prefer oldest soft reservations (best-effort) then fall back to size-based. sound ok?
aj: +1
sam: +1 but add a metric so we can tune thresholds.
cheng: I'll update the RFC with the ledger semantics, the event schema, and a heartbeat sketch. will also prototype local escrow behavior in the prefactor branch.
deploy-bot: build 0.72.3 started on branch `prefactor/escrow-ledger` (CI #3421)
maria: thanks. can we aim to freeze the shape by EOD Friday for engineering to implement?
cheng: yup, will circulate a PR today with explicit pseudocode for `reserve()`/`release()` and the heartbeat frequency.
aj: sounds good. I'll review the PR and validate perf impact.
alex: I'll add telemetry dashboards for allocation deltas and failed-move counts.
maria: great — keep the thread updated with PR link. :thumbsup:
